title: BroadcastLogHistory
description: What the publisher and the readers of one broadcast-log stress run observed (ADR 0062 section 5). Every backend's stress run writes this form and `sce-codegen check-broadcast-history` judges it, so one linearizability checker serves all of them. A participant is one thread or goroutine; its operations are listed in its program order. Every operation carries two readings of ONE clock that all participants share, taken immediately before the call (`invoked`) and immediately after it returned (`returned`); a counter that each participant increments atomically at both points is such a clock, and gives distinct readings. An operation that returned before another was invoked is ordered before it; operations that overlap may be ordered either way. The history is linearizable when its operations can be put in one sequence that keeps that order and is a run of the sequential bounded log of `retention` entries: `h` entries published, only the last `retention` retained; a reader owns a cursor that `open` sets and `read` moves.

version.description: The version of this format. A reader that meets another refuses the file.

retention.description: The retention of the sequential log the run is judged against: the number of entries a reader may rely on, which the log under test was built with. The ring under test holds one slot more.

publisher.description: The one publisher's operations in its program order: publishes, and reads of the head.

readers.description: One list per reader, in that reader's program order. A read needs an earlier open of the same reader.

Operation.description: One observed operation. A publish names its `value` and the sequence number `seq` it took, which is its position among the publisher's publishes. An open names where the cursor was asked to start (`from`: `oldest`, `head`, or `at` with the sequence number `at`) and the `cursor` it set. A read names its `outcome`: `item` (the entry `seq` that held `value`), `empty` (the cursor was at the head) or `lagged` (the cursor was `skipped` entries below the start of the window, and moved to it). A head names the number it returned.

invoked.description: The clock reading taken immediately before the call.

returned.description: The clock reading taken immediately after the call returned. Later than `invoked`, and earlier than the same participant's next `invoked`.
